day: The Exaltation of the Holy Cross ‐ Feast
text:
There is something profound in how God meets us in our despair. In the wilderness, the people turn away in complaint and fear, and God responds not with abandonment but with a remedy. A serpent—the very image of what threatens them—becomes the means of their healing. They need only look.

Jesus tells Nicodemus that he himself must be lifted up the same way. The cross, which looks like death and failure, becomes the place where we find life. It is not a punishment hidden from view but a sign meant to be seen, contemplated, believed in. Just as the ancient Israelites had to turn their gaze toward the bronze serpent, we are invited to look upon Christ lifted up and to trust what we see there: that we are loved, that we are saved, that God wants not our condemnation but our life.

The readings ask us today simply to remember. To recall that God has never abandoned us, even when we have lost patience or faith. To look, even now, at the cross and see there not judgment but mercy—the full measure of love poured out for a world God refuses to condemn.

Perhaps you might sit quietly with that image today: the lifted cross, and what it means that God chose that way to show us we are loved.
